standard.title: Create and present texts for diverse contexts
standard.description: create and present informative and imaginative texts for diverse contexts and purposes, selecting vocabulary, expressions, sentence structures and textual features and conventions to engage different audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create and present extended multimodal texts with language manipulation, drafting and editing processes (AC9LCH8C05). They have produced community-facing texts with deliberate stylistic choices. They have not yet produced evaluative and persuasive writing at extended length, created procedural texts, produced literary or reflective texts for publication, or selected and applied conventions from specific literary styles.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and present informative and imaginative texts for diverse contexts and purposes — selecting vocabulary, expressions, sentence structures and conventions deliberately to engage different audiences — including evaluative, persuasive, procedural and literary forms.

nodes.label: Evaluative and persuasive writing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce evaluative and persuasive texts — reviews, debates, analytical responses, advocacy pieces — selecting language and structure deliberately to make a case.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce an evaluative or persuasive text of at least ten sentences using at least three persuasive structures and demonstrating a clear position supported by evidence or reasoning.
nodes.typical_width: Produce evaluative writing — reviews, analytical responses, feedback; write and debate persuasive texts on a range of topics; use evidence, logical structure and persuasive language; create texts for school newspapers and community publications; analyse and evaluate pros and cons of issues.
wider: Produce an extended persuasive text on a topic of genuine personal significance — with a documented drafting and revision process showing deliberate language choices

Compare persuasive text conventions in target language and English — identify how argument structure, evidence presentation and rhetorical strategies differ, and apply target language conventions authentically
nodes.hinge_reason: Evaluative and persuasive writing is the foundational productive capability for the full range of texts this descriptor requires. Students who can only produce narrative or informative texts cannot meet the evaluative, argumentative and procedural demands that follow.

response_modes.reason: Persuasive and evaluative texts require deliberate structural planning before drafting — students need to identify their position, organise evidence, and select appropriate language before producing. Explicit argument structure instruction followed by scaffolded writing practice builds this planning capacity.

success_criteria: Produces an evaluative or persuasive text with a clear position supported by evidence
Uses at least three persuasive structures across the text

nodes.label: Procedural and community texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create procedural texts and community-facing informative materials in target language, applying appropriate conventions for each text type.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one procedural text (e.g. evacuation procedure, application checklist, operational guide) and at least one community-facing informative text using correct target language conventions for each.
nodes.typical_width: Create procedural texts — evacuation protocols, application procedures, lab checklists; produce texts for school or community newspapers; create cultural awareness resources; produce multimodal bilingual community texts; apply text-type conventions appropriately throughout.
wider: Create a complete procedural and informational resource for a real community need — evaluate its usability with an intended audience and revise
Compare procedural text conventions in target language and English — identify where the structural and linguistic conventions differ and apply the target language conventions correctly

response_modes.reason: Procedural and community text creation requires understanding of varied genre conventions. Practice across different procedural text types — emergency, operational, application — builds the flexible genre knowledge needed before students can apply conventions independently.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Community-facing text production for real audiences — particularly in bilingual community contexts — is the highest-authenticity creation context for background learners. Width investment here produces texts with genuine real-world use and positions students as bilingual community contributors.
success_criteria: Creates a procedural text applying correct genre conventions throughout
Creates a community-facing informative text appropriate for its specified audience

nodes.label: Literary and stylistically distinctive texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create literary and imaginative texts in target language that apply stylistic conventions, demonstrate personal voice, and engage audiences through deliberate language and structural choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a literary or stylistically distinctive text that applies at least two conventions from a specific literary style or genre, demonstrating deliberate vocabulary and structural choices.
nodes.typical_width: Create imaginative stories about self and identity; use literary style models; produce narrative texts with logical structure; create texts using literary devices to enhance emotional impact; create Acknowledgements of Country/Place; write texts for diverse formats and audiences.
wider: Create a text that consciously applies the conventions of a specific target language literary genre — annotate the stylistic choices made and explain how each serves the text's purpose
Produce a text using a literary style model and then evaluate its success — identify where the model conventions were applied effectively and where the student's own voice emerged

response_modes.reason: Literary and stylistic text production integrates persuasive writing skills (node 1) and genre knowledge (node 2) into the fullest expression of creative capability at this level. The teaching investment is in creating genuine literary engagement — students as authors with a vision, not only as genre conformers.

success_criteria: Creates a literary or stylistically distinctive text applying at least two conventions from a specific style or genre
Demonstrates deliberate vocabulary and structural choices that serve the text's purpose
